title: React Project-Based Learning Core Check
description: Check your understanding of project requirements, component architecture, milestones, acceptance criteria, extensions, and tradeoffs.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What should define the scope of a project before coding?
questions.explanation: Project lessons begin with goals, requirements, and acceptance criteria.

questions.prompt: In the Todo app project, why split components such as input, list, and item?

options.text: To keep responsibilities clear and easier to test

questions.explanation: Suggested component architectures separate responsibilities into focused pieces.

questions.prompt: What issue does the Weather Dashboard lesson call out around fast repeated searches?

options.text: Stale responses arriving out of order

questions.explanation: Async projects must handle stale or out-of-order responses.

questions.prompt: What is a key requirement in an e-commerce cart?
questions.explanation: Cart projects center on correct cart actions, quantities, totals, and edge cases.

questions.prompt: Which are useful project milestones? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Ignoring manual testing until after launch

questions.explanation: Milestones break a project into reviewable increments such as UI, state, data, and polish.

questions.prompt: Why write a manual test script for a project?

options.text: To verify important user flows and edge cases consistently

questions.explanation: Manual test scripts make project validation repeatable.

questions.prompt: What is an extension idea in project-based learning?

options.text: A non-essential enhancement after core requirements work
A bug that blocks the first milestone
A replacement for the project goal

questions.explanation: Extensions add stretch value after the core project is complete.

questions.prompt: A project README checklist can help communicate setup, features, tradeoffs, and known limitations.
questions.explanation: The project module encourages documenting how the app works and what decisions were made.
